title: Agreement with the deterministic simulation
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine, let $\text{oracle}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be an input bit string, let $\beta$ be a Boolean value, and let $a$ be an initial configuration. Suppose that at every time $t<T$, whenever the deterministic simulation that replaces each choice instruction by the answer $\beta$ is in a control state $l$, the instruction of $A$ at $l$ is not a choice instruction. Then for every finite choice string $\sigma$ of length at most $T$, the nondeterministic run on $\sigma$ agrees with that deterministic simulation after $|\sigma|$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle and input bit string
At every $t<T$, each control state reached by the deterministic simulation has a non-choice instruction
A finite choice string $\sigma$ with length at most $T$
